findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but the only method inherited from UsernamePasswordForm is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) at UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 and no no-arg overload exists in UsernameForm, UsernamePasswordForm, or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator. This is a compilation failure. It should be called as isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()).

findings.title: Requiring a known user breaks initial discoverable-passkey login
findings.body: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) now requires user != null, and authenticate() at line 115 and challenge(context,error,field) at line 137 use it to decide whether to call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context). On the initial login page no user is known yet, which is exactly the discoverable/resident-key passkey flow that identifies the user from the credential, so fillContextForm is never called, the conditional-UI challenge/autocomplete data is not rendered, and passwordless login from UsernamePasswordForm is broken. The same applies after a failed initial password attempt, where bad-password handling clears the user before challenge() re-renders the form. Previously fillContextForm was called when the user was not yet selected. The guard should be based on passkeys being enabled, not on a user already being present; the known-user check is only relevant to showing that user's authenticators.

findings.title: Always hiding WebAuthn authenticators defeats the no-credential guard for known users
findings.body: shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() now unconditionally returns false, so WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm() never builds WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean and never takes its empty-authenticators early return at WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:104-107. Combined with UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() checking only the realm passkeys flag and user != null (not whether that user is configured for a passwordless credential), a re-authenticating user with no passkey credential will still be rendered the conditional-UI/WebAuthn form even though no credential can succeed. This contradicts the stated expectation in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey that users without a passkey should not see WebAuthn elements; that test only covers realm-level passkeys disabled, not the passkeys-enabled/user-without-credential case.
